steps.submitted_work: Let u = x^2, dv = cos(x)dx => du = 2x dx, v = sin(x)
steps.expected_rubric_step: Identify parts u and dv correctly: u = x^2, dv = cos(x)dx
Apply integration by parts formula: uv - \int v du
Perform second iteration: u = 2x, dv = sin(x)dx => v = -cos(x). Apply uv - \int v du with outer negative.
steps.divergence_reason: Sign error on expanding inner bracket. Minus sign was inverted across the -\int term.

steps.expected_rubric_step: Final simplified antiderivative with constant: x^2 sin(x) + 2x cos(x) - 2sin(x) + C
steps.divergence_reason: Omitted integration constant + C and final term sign affected by Step 3 leak.

forensic_summary: Method selection was sound. Divergence occurred at Step 3 due to negative sign distribution across inner brackets during the 2nd iteration of Integration by Parts. Missing +C on final line.
